subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing — follow up & numbers requested
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@finai.co>, Jacob Ross <j.ross@finai.co>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12T21:05:00Z
Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing — follow up & numbers requested

Hi Olivia / Jacob —

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation and appreciate the level of detail on your infra and latency needs. As discussed, I want to capture the numbers we need to scope Dedicated (reserved) capacity and give a back-of-envelope cost estimate. Would you confirm the items below when you have a moment?

1) Volume & growth
   - Current expected monthly token volume (month 0): — you mentioned roughs but can you confirm a target number (tokens/month)?
   - 6–12 month growth target (tokens/month)

2) Traffic shape / throughput
   - Average requests per second (RPS) during business hours and peak RPS
   - Average response size (tokens per response) and max sequence/context length you expect

3) Latency & SLOs
   - P50 / P95 latency targets for generation (e.g., <150ms p50, <300ms p95)

4) Budget & unit economics
   - Monthly budget range for Dedicated (reserved) capacity?
   - If you have a target $/1M tokens we should aim for, please share (helps map to GPU counts and reserved pricing)

5) Constraints / preferences
   - Preferred GPU family (H100 vs. A100) or willingness to use quantized variants / smaller model for cost savings
   - Any data residency / VPC requirements we should bake into the proposal

If you want, I can share a short spreadsheet that maps tokens -> GPUs -> estimated $/1M tokens (back-of-envelope) and a couple of configuration options (base reserved + peak burst pool). Attaching our standard Dedicated pricing overview for reference.

Next steps: once we have the numbers above I’ll loop in Vivek (cc’d) to translate into throughput / GPU recommendations and we’ll send a 2-option proposal (cost-first and latency-first).

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0104

Marissa —

Thanks — below are the numbers we can confirm today (happy to refine):

1) Volume & growth
   - Month 0 (launch): ~400M tokens/month
   - 6 months: 900M tokens/month

2) Traffic shape / throughput
   - Avg RPS (business hours): 40–50 req/s
   - Peak RPS (short bursts): 140–160 req/s (couple of times/day)
   - Avg response size: ~320 tokens (some queries go up to 1,200 tokens occasionally)

3) Latency & SLOs
   - Target: p95 <= 300ms for our core chat flow (ideally lower for short prompts)

4) Budget & unit economics
   - Early budget: $25k–40k / month for Dedicated (we can stretch for SLA/latency needs)
   - Target unit cost: ideally <= $350 / 1M tokens (we know this is aggressive, but want to understand tradeoffs)

5) Constraints / preferences
   - Prefer H100 if it meaningfully reduces latency; open to A100 if it helps cost but need to see numbers
   - VPC and basic audit logs required (we’ll follow up on SOC2 items separately)

I’ll attach a simple forecast for next 6 months — it’s coarse but should help.

Olivia
Head of Product, FinAI
olivia@finai.co

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing — follow up & numbers requested

Thanks Olivia — this is perfect and very helpful. Below are two quick, back-of-envelope configurations based on your numbers (we’ll refine with Vivek):

Assumptions used for calc (example model: 70B-class chat model, mixed precision):
 - Avg response: 320 tokens
 - 30 days/month
 - Baseline throughput numbers per GPU are approximate — we’ll validate with perf runs but useful for planning

Option A — Cost-first (target <= $350 / 1M tokens)
 - Initial target: 400M tokens/month
 - Recommended reserved: 2 x H100 (baseline) + burst pool (autoscale) up to 5 GPUs during peak
 - Expected sustained throughput with 2x H100: ~65–90 req/s (depending on batching)
 - Burst capacity covers your peak 140–160 req/s spikes
 - Estimated unit cost: ~ $320–$370 / 1M tokens (depends on utilization and batching)

Option B — Latency-first (target p95 <= 300ms)
 - Recommended reserved: 3 x H100 + burst to 6 GPUs
 - Expected sustained throughput: ~110–140 req/s with lower queuing; p95 within your target for <=1k token responses
 - Estimated unit cost: ~ $450 / 1M tokens (higher due to more reserved capacity but better tail latency)

Notes / tradeoffs:
 - Using A100 instead of H100 reduces reserved monthly cost but increases latency / reduces tokens/sec per GPU — may push you toward larger reserved counts.
 - Quantized model variants (e.g., 4-bit / optimized kernels) can reduce GPU memory and increase effective throughput — we can include in a second pass.

Next steps: Vivek, can you confirm the tokens/sec per GPU numbers you’d expect for the model family Olivia mentioned (and whether A100/Ampere perf numbers change the guidance)? After that we’ll prepare a 2-option commercial (monthly reserved price + burst pricing + expected $/1M tokens) and share a one-pager we can use in procurement conversations.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0104
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing — follow up & numbers requested

Hi all — looping in some perf guidance from the infra side (high-level):

Model family/context: 70B-class chat model (FP16) — numbers are approximate and based on our internal benchmarks with batching and KV cache enabled. We’ll run a tailored perf test against your prompt shapes to firm these up.

Throughput / GPU (approx):
 - H100 (fp16): 1 GPU ~ 400–600 tokens/sec (conservative; depends on batch size & seq length)
 - A100 (fp16): 1 GPU ~ 220–350 tokens/sec
 - If you use a quantized 4-bit runtime (where supported), effective tokens/sec can increase ~1.2–1.5x

Mapping to Olivia’s numbers (avg 320 tokens/resp):
 - 400M tokens/month => ~13.3M tokens/day => ~154 tokens/sec average across 24h
 - With H100 single-GPU at 500 tokens/sec, 1 GPU could cover average load with headroom — but peak burst handling and latency targets push us to reserved multiple GPUs + burst pool.

Practical recommendation:
 - Start with 2x H100 reserved to guarantee capacity and p95 goals. Autoscale pool for peak spikes (we can size burst based on your forecasted peak windows).
 - If procurement prefers A100 for budget reasons, plan on adding ~1.5–2x GPUs to keep equivalent headroom.

I’ll schedule a short perf run with your team (we’ll need sample prompts and a short window to run synthetic load) to validate these numbers and produce a tighter cost / $ per 1M token estimate.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
